#refs: art/source/tram-stop_svantnerova.jpg ; art/masters/bg_natural/S11_src_t3g-dubravka_jakubowski-2018.jpg ; art/source/rooms/S11/svantnerova-stop-ne-platform_kartaview-2021-04.jpg
#style: art/backgrounds/sokolikova-street.png
Place: the Svantnerova tram stop on the Dubravka - Karlova Ves tram line in Bratislava-Dubravka (Slovakia), on the south-west platform, looking north-west along the platform. The double tram track runs in the middle of a wide street: the west carriageway lies below the platform on the left, a grass strip, the east carriageway and a low 1980s shopping pavilion are on the right, and 8- to 12-storey prefabricated panel tower blocks stand behind the trees. Image 2 is a 2022 photo taken on this platform (use it for the geography: the track and the road beside the platform, the railings, the panel towers and trees; its modern glass shelter, display board and paving did NOT exist in 1995). Image 3 is a red-cream Tatra T3 tram on this Dubravka line (use it for the tram's shape and livery only). Image 4 shows the same stop from the road (railings, towers).

Brief: the Dubravka tram stop in June 1995, early on a sunny summer morning: warm low morning sunlight from the right behind the camera, long soft shadows falling forward to the left, fresh green lindens. The ORIGINAL 1980s stop: a long shelter of brown-painted steel tubes bent into arches (each arch rises from the platform at the back, curves over the top and comes down to the platform at the front), a solid brown back wall of vertical boards along the road side, a translucent light-blue curved plastic roof, a wooden slat bench along the inside of the back wall; the platform paved with big grey concrete slabs and a light, almost white edge strip along the track. An old red-cream Tatra T3 tram (cream upper body, windows and roof edge, red lower body, round headlights) stands at the platform with its doors closed; its route box above the windscreen is blank, no number, no destination text. 1995 details: a colourful 1990s advertising poster with abstract shapes (no lettering) hangs in the first arch, a paper timetable in a glazed case, no electronic display anywhere, no tactile paving.

Camera: eye level about 2 m above the platform, looking along the platform in one-point perspective; the horizon is at y 400 and the platform's long lines meet at x ~1060 on it. Keep this exact geometry from the sketch: the platform from the bottom edge to the vanishing point, its light edge strip from (1449, 1080) to the vanishing point, the near rail from (1750, 1080) to the vanishing point, the shelter's back wall from x 380 (near end, y 405-805) receding to x ~950, the front tubes standing at x 690 (near) and further back, the stop post standing at x 787 with its foot at y 812, the tram's front face at x 1273-1587, y 274-620.

What the sketch blocks are, left to right: far left the west carriageway (asphalt) below the platform with white zebra-crossing stripes at the near left, a lawn verge with young lindens and a long 4-storey panel block beyond it; the low concrete wall with a steel railing along the platform's road side; the short ramp at the near left where the railing has a gap; the long brown tube shelter with its solid brown back wall, translucent blue roof, the poster in the first arch and the bench; the stop post with the clock on top, a small stop plate and the timetable case; the platform; the light edge strip; the double track on ballast with concrete sleepers; the red-cream tram on the near track with its pantograph up on the overhead wire; grey traction poles; beyond the track a grass strip, the east carriageway, the shopping pavilion (glass shopfronts, flat roof, no signs) and the panel towers; blue sky with a few small clouds.

Interactive props - each painted clearly inside its block, the same size as its block, easy to recognise at a glance:
1. {rect:S11.ambient 1}: the glazed timetable case on the grey stop post, white paper inside printed with neat columns of illegible tiny print (no digits); above it on the post a small white stop plate with a red border and a simple tram pictogram (no words), and on top of the post a round clock with a polished brass frame and a white dial with black hour ticks (no numerals), the hands showing about five past eight.
2. {rect:S11.ambient 2}: the wooden slat bench inside the shelter along the back wall, seat and backrest of warm brown slats on black steel legs; two small pink chewing-gum blobs stuck under the front edge of the seat.
{exit:S11.to_S12} is the short concrete ramp at the near left where the railing has a gap, leading down to the zebra crossing (towards the school); the concrete kerb corner where the platform edge meets the ramp has a small chipped-off corner. {exit:S11.to_S18} is the far end of the platform beyond the shelter. {exit:S11.to_S19} is the tram itself, standing at the platform.

Walkable floor: the open platform in front of the shelter and to the right of it (within {walk}, except the shelter, its tubes and the stop post at its left edge, which stay exactly as in the sketch) is grey concrete slabs - one continuous flat surface with no kerb, step, edge or change of material inside it, and nothing else standing on it: no bins, no extra posts, no benches, no bags, no people. Only morning light, long shadows and fine joints between the slabs.

Fiction rules: a generic Dubravka stop: no stop name, no transport-company logos, no line numbers, no route or destination text, no readable timetable; no shop signs or brands on the pavilion; no billboards with text; no car number plates. No people anywhere (no driver or passengers visible in the tram - its windows reflect the sky), no animals, no cars on the roads. Any paper shows only illegible scribbles, no digits.
